finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /hooks/test sends a server-side POST to an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL (req.body.callback) with no scheme, host, or IP allowlist, and returns the upstream status code. Enables internal/metadata probing and POSTing to internal services. Severity HIGH (MEDIUM if the pub router is mounted behind auth, which is not visible in this file).

trace.note: pub.post('/hooks/test') route handler; no auth middleware on pub router in this file
req.body.callback passed directly as axios target URL; no parsing or validation
upstream status code returned to caller, giving a reachability oracle

finding.guards_checked: No scheme check, no URL parsing or .hostname comparison, no allowlist, no auth/authz middleware on pub route in this file. URL is per-request, so literal/env/config exemptions do not apply. axios follows redirects by default (redirect risk: yes). Caveat: pub router mount point and mount-time auth not visible; DEPLOY-REC webhook-engine exemption cannot be ruled in or out from this code alone.

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:19-22 has no URL parsing, scheme check, hostname or allowlist check, or auth middleware. requireAdmin (routes.js:7-12) is attached only to `admin` (routes.js:12), not `pub`. The directory has no file that mounts `pub` or defines a DEPLOY-REC exemption, so mount-time auth and the webhook-engine exemption cannot be checked here.
verdict.reason: At routes.js:20 `axios.post(req.body.callback, ...)` passes an unauthenticated request body field straight to an outbound request, and routes.js:21 returns the upstream status, with no closing guard in routes.js:19-22. The one unresolved item is whether the router is mounted behind auth elsewhere, which is outside this directory and affects severity, not the code-level finding.

finding.claim: Admin-only GET /diagnostics/fetch sends a server-side GET to an arbitrary URL from req.query.url with no allowlist, and returns the upstream status code. Admin authentication does not close SSRF to metadata or RFC-1918 targets. Severity MEDIUM.
finding.source: req.query.url (routes.js:15), attacker-controlled query parameter reachable only with an admin session

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) gates all routes on the admin router
req.query.url passed directly into axios GET with no validation
upstream status code returned, so result is not fully blind

finding.guards_checked: Role check only (routes.js:8, :12). No scheme, host, or IP allowlist. Admin router mount point not visible in this file. Redirects followed by default (redirect risk: yes). Separated from SSRF-1 because access control differs.

verdict.guard_found: none closing. Role check only: routes.js:8 (requireAdmin) applied via routes.js:12 (admin.use). No scheme, host, or IP validation before routes.js:15.
verdict.reason: All trace lines match routes.js:8, 12, 14, 15, 16, but the source does not meet the bar: req.query.url at routes.js:15 is reachable only after requireAdmin (routes.js:8) confirms req.session.role === 'admin', so no unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker can control it. The candidate's own claim concedes this. Admin-only SSRF is a separate, lower-severity hardening issue, not a finding under this rubric.
